2012_039_081412regmtg.paragraph: Troy School District Board of Education packet for the Regular Meeting of August 14, 2012 at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. It carries the July 10, 2012 minutes (Resolutions 12-070 through 12-077), Treasurer's Reports for June and July 2012 with fund summary budget reports and check registers, eight new teacher hires, a report on Michigan's NCLB waiver, and the selection of an architect ahead of a potential November 2013 bond issue. Under the waiver approved July 19, 2012, twelve Troy schools were identified as Focus Schools, four as Reward Schools and two as Continuous Improvement Schools, with no Priority Schools in the district.

Regular Meeting, August 14, 2012, 7:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. ## Personnel, curriculum, business
Probationary contracts recommended for Kerry Brennan (Wattles), Cheryl Buxton (Hamilton), Ryan Irla (AP Economics, Athens), Jessica Jarrard (.5 FTE Social Worker, Services Building), Matthew Mooney (Barnard), William Ris (Physics, Athens), Chris Schoonover (History, Athens) and Amy Schwarb (Early Childhood Preschool-ASD, Niles Continuing Education).

Anne Mull reported on Michigan's NCLB waiver, approved July 19, 2012, which replaces the 100%-proficient-by-2014 requirement with Annual Measurable Objectives using 2011-2012 as the baseline and ten more years to reach 85% proficiency. Focus Schools: Athens, Baker, Boulan, Larson, Smith, Troy Union, Morse, Hamilton, Leonard, Bemis, Barnard, Wattles. Continuous Improvement: Martell, Troy High School. Reward: Costello, Hill, Schroeder, Wass.

Mark Rajter reported on the architectural/engineering RFP for a potential November 2013 Bond Issue Election covering roofs, parking lots, building mechanicals and related technology, and operations and maintenance equipment. Fourteen firms attended the July 9 pre-submittal conference, ten submitted proposals, six were interviewed, and TMP Architecture Inc. was selected. Also on the agenda: the MASB Region 8 ballot and a closed session under Public Act 267, Section 8 (h).

NCLB WAIVER IMPLICATIONS (item 7.B), presented by Mrs. Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment; no action required. The ESEA/NCLB Adequate Yearly Progress rule required 100% of students proficient in mathematics and reading by 2014; Michigan received waiver approval July 19, 2012. New Annual Measurable Objectives use the 2011-2012 school year as the baseline and allow another 10 years to reach 85% proficiency. The original nine subgroups are retained (six ethnicities, students with IEPs, English Language Learners, economically disadvantaged) and a bottom 30% subgroup is added. Troy has no Priority Schools; Focus Schools are Athens, Baker, Boulan, Larson, Smith, Troy Union, Morse, Hamilton, Leonard, Bemis, Barnard and Wattles; Continuous Improvement Schools are Martell and Troy High School; Reward Schools are Costello, Hill, Schroeder and Wass. Reward status reflects the top 5% of the Top-to-Bottom ranking, the top 5% on improvement, or 'Beating the Odds'; Focus status reflects the gap between top 30% and bottom 30% average scale scores. The Michigan Department of Education will supply a District Toolkit and District Improvement Facilitators; a district still reporting Focus Schools in 2013/14 will purchase the facilitator's services. Reporting shifts to green, red or yellow by subject, with a 95% participation requirement.

ARCHITECTURAL AND ENGINEERING SERVICES (item 8.A), presented by Mark Rajter; no action required. The RFP sought a firm to assess facilities and set scope for a potential November 2013 Bond Issue election, limited to roofs, parking lots, building mechanicals and related technology, and operations and maintenance equipment. RFPs were issued June 27, 2012, with a pre-submittal conference July 9, proposals due July 13, interviews July 17-19, and scope of work due to the Board October 16, 2012. Fourteen firms attended the pre-submittal conference and ten submitted proposals; the committee was Mark Rajter, Ken Miller, Executive Director of Facilities, and Sara Konieczka, Purchasing Supervisor. Six firms were interviewed: French Associates, Integrated Design Solutions, Kingscott Associates, NTH Consultants Ltd., SHW Group and TMP Architecture Inc. Scoring used a 100 point scale: 5 background, 15 staffing, 15 work load, 40 related project experience, 20 management summary, 5 location. TMP was chosen, with facility evaluation scheduled from August 15 through October 9.

MASB ELECTION (item 10.A): a ballot for one Region 8 candidate for a three-year term on the 2012 Michigan Association of School Boards' Board of Directors, though the header reads 2011. Candidates: Robert Kirby, Wyandotte Public Schools, Wayne County (11 years); Roderick Means, Westwood Community School District, Wayne County (16 years); Earl C. Rickman, Mount Clemens Community School District, Macomb County (28 years; MASB Director from 1995 until 2012; past President of the National School Boards Association); and incumbent Keith Warnick, Ferndale Public Schools, Oakland County (eight years on the board, three on the MASB board). CLOSED SESSION (item 11.A): a resolution under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (h) to discuss an attorney-client privilege item, roll call of Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt and Underwood.
